As temperatures rise, so does the desire to escape to places where summer feels a little more relaxed. Germany’s low mountain ranges offer ideal conditions: dense forests provide shade, higher elevations bring pleasantly fresh air, and lakes and rivers invite visitors to take a refreshing break.

[![](https://www.germany.travel/media/resources/img/logo-google.svg)\\
Give “germany.travel” priority on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=germany.travel "Give “germany.travel” priority on Google")

The trend known as a “coolcation” responds to exactly this desire: travelling to regions that promise nature-based relaxation even on warm days. From the volcanic crater lakes of the Eifel to the karst caves of the Swabian Alb, these twelve destinations reveal just how varied a summer in Germany’s low mountain ranges can be.

## Sauerland: Lakes meet fresh mountain air

![Sauerland landscape with meadows and forest](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/kampagne/feelgood/0_feelgood_2024/zertifizierte_reiseziele/sommer_im_sauerland2_sauerland-tourismus_e.v._klaus-peter_kappest_react-eu.jpg)**Sauerland** ©Sauerland-Tourismus e.V (Peter Kappest)

Between Lake Biggesee, Lake Diemelsee and Lake Hennesee, wooded shores, bathing spots and wide expanses of water create a varied landscape. Rising above them is the Kahler Asten, whose higher elevations often remain pleasantly fresh even on warm summer days. Those exploring the **[Rothaarsteig](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/rothaarsteig.html "Rothaarsteig")** hike for long stretches through shady forests and enjoy sweeping views across the upland scenery. In this way, the **[Sauerland](https://www.sauerland.com/en "Sauerland")** combines nature, exercise and refreshing summer air.

## Eifel: Where volcanoes now provide refreshment

![Bird`s eye view of the Pulvermaar crater lake, surrounded by autumn-colored forest and wide fields under a blue sky with loose clouds](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/adobestock_360279248.jpeg)**Pulvermaar in the Vulkaneifel** ©Adobe Stock (AWL Images)

Where volcanoes once shaped the landscape, deep-blue crater lakes now lie between wooded hills. The Pulvermaar, Gemündener Maar and Schalkenmehrener Maar are among the most impressive reminders of the region’s geological past. In **[Eifel National Park](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/eifel-national-park.html "Eifel National Park")**, extensive forests offer welcome shade, while Lake Rursee provides opportunities to enjoy summer by the water. The combination of volcanic scenery and unspoilt nature makes the **[region](https://www.eifel.info/en/ "region")** an exceptional destination for warm days.

## Swabian Alb: Pleasantly cool underground

![Eine Frau sitzt in einem Boot in der Wimsener Höhle in Hayingen. Sie blickt zur Höhlendecke hinauf. Das Wasser in der Höhle ist klar. Das Licht von draußen erhellt einen Teil der Höhle.](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/_20z5446.jpg)**Hayingen: Woman visits the water cave Wimsener Höhle in a boat** ©DZT (Florian Trykowski)

The **[UNESCO Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/unesco-swabian-alb-biosphere-reserve.html "UNESCO Swabian Alb Biosphere Reserve")** combines panoramic plateaus with a fascinating karst landscape. Water and rock define the scenery at the Blautopf spring, in the Danube Valley and at Urach Waterfall. Underground, the temperatures are particularly refreshing: the Nebelhöhle and Wimsener Höhle caves remain cool throughout the year. These impressive caves add another dimension to the region’s varied natural attractions.

## Odenwald: Forests, river valleys and historic towns

![Ein orangefarbener Waggon fährt in der Nähe einer Bergstation der Königstuhlbahn und Standseilbahn, mit einer schönen Aussicht auf die Stadt Heidelberg.](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/staedte_kultur_content/heidelberg/look_71382422.jpg)**Heidelberg: Königstuhlbahn mountain station and funicular railway** ©Lookphotos (Hanna Wagner)

Shady mixed forests, gentle uplands and the River Neckar shape the **[Odenwald](https://en.hessen-tourismus.de/where-to-go/regions/bergstrasse-odenwald "Odenwald")**. The landscape is particularly impressive at the sweeping bend of the Neckar near Eberbach, while the Felsenmeer in the Lautertal valley offers a striking contrast with its massive granite boulders. Half-timbered villages and historic old towns lend the region additional character, combining natural experiences with culture.

## Palatinate: Summer beneath Germany’s largest forest

![Eine große Felsformation steht im Naturpark Pfälzerwald, Lambrecht, umgeben von grünen Bäumen und Sträuchern](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/_grj8638.jpg)**Lambrecht: Pfälzerwald Nature Park** ©DZT (Francesco Carovillano)

The **[Palatinate Forest](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/unesco-palatinate-forest-north-vosges-biosphere-reserve.html "Palatinate Forest")** is the largest continuous forested area in Germany. Beneath its dense canopy, many places remain pleasantly cool even at the height of summer. Among distinctive red sandstone formations and wooded hills, the Dahner Felsenland offers varied hiking trails and constantly changing views. Those seeking tranquillity and nature will find ideal conditions here for relaxed summer days.

## Bavarian Forest: Wild nature and peaceful mountain lakes

![The course of the river meanders through dense green forest with tall conifers, surrounded by wooded hills under a dramatic sky with large clouds](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/_weg5646_bn.jpg)**River Teisnach in the Bavarian Forest** ©DZT (Jens Wegener)

With its pristine forests and clear mountain lakes, the Bavarian Forest reveals its close-to-nature character. **[Bavarian Forest National Park](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/bavarian-forest-national-park.html "Bavarian Forest National Park")** protects vast woodland areas where nature is largely free to develop undisturbed. Lake Großer Arbersee and Lake Rachelsee lie between forested mountain slopes and invite visitors to pause and cool down. The higher elevations also contribute to the region’s fresh summer climate.

## Steigerwald: Ancient beech trees and peaceful trails

![The course of the river meanders through dense green forest with tall conifers, surrounded by wooded hills under a dramatic sky with large clouds](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/_weg5646_bn.jpg)**River Teisnach in the Bavarian Forest** ©DZT (Jens Wegener)

Mighty beech trees and gentle hills define the scenery of the **[Steigerwald](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/nature-park-steigerwald.html "Steigerwald")**. The Ebrach Forest is particularly atmospheric, with its ancient woodland creating a peaceful, almost primeval setting. Those who explore the area at a leisurely pace can experience the interplay of light and shade beneath the treetops particularly intensely, far from large crowds.

## Hunsrück-Nahe: Fresh breezes on the uplands

![Green trees and wooded hills in the Hunsrück-Hochwald National Park stretch out to the horizon in a soft light](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/kampagne/feelgood/erlebnisangebote/aktiv_in_der_natur/_grg6169.jpg)**Hunsrück-Hochwald National Park: View over the Erbeskopf mountain range** ©DZT (Francesco Carovillano)

Broad ridges and extensive forests give the Hunsrück a pleasantly fresh climate, even in summer. In **[Hunsrück-Hochwald National Park](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/hunsrueck-hochwald-national-park.html "Hunsrück-Hochwald National Park")**, near-natural woodland alternates with open viewpoints. From the Erbeskopf, the highest point in the region, the view stretches far across the forested upland landscape. It is an ideal destination for anyone wishing to combine outdoor activity with milder temperatures.

## Thuringian Forest: Along the Rennsteig

![Panoramic view of the Schönbrunn dam, a reservoir surrounded by wooded hills in Schleusengrund](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/img_2783.jpg)**Schönbrunn Dam in Schleusegrund** ©Thüringer Tourismus GmbH (Melf Mäder)

The **[Rennsteig](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/rennsteig.html "Rennsteig")** runs for many kilometres through shady forests and is one of Germany’s best-known high-level hiking trails. Along the route, springs, streams and panoramic uplands alternate. The Schneekopf, Schwarzatal, Vesser Valley and the Lütschetal and Schönbrunn reservoirs add further variety. In the **[Thuringian Forest](https://www.thueringer-wald.com/en/w/opendata/destination/thuringian-woodland "Thuringian Forest")**, one refreshing landscape follows another.

## Spessart: In the shade of ancient deciduous forests

![View across the meadow to the Spessart mountains](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/spessart_fernblick_oberhalb_weiperz_und_breunings.jpg)**Distant view above Weiperz and Breunings in the Spessart** ©Spessart Tourismus und Marketing GmbH (Claus Tews)

The **[Spessart](https://en.hessen-tourismus.de/where-to-go/regions/spessart "Spessart")** is one of Germany’s largest continuous areas of deciduous woodland. Dense tree canopies line many hiking trails and create a cool microclimate. In the Spessart Nature Park and Hafenlohr Valley, peaceful forest paths alternate with small streams, while Lake Wiesbüttsee provides an inviting place to relax by the water.

## Bergisches Land: A waterside escape close to the city

![Müngstener Brücke, die höchste Eisenbahnbrücke Deutschlands, überspannt ein üppig grünes Tal zwischen Remscheid und Solingen, unter dem der Fluss Wupper fließt.](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/adobestock_69081463.jpeg)**Solingen: Sommer an der Müngstener Brücke** ©Adobe Stock (Thomas Jablonski)

Just a short journey from Cologne or Düsseldorf, reservoirs, forests and gentle uplands shape the scenery of the **[Bergisches Land](https://www.nrw-tourism.com/regions/bergisches-land "Bergisches Land")**. The Dhünn, Wupper and Agger reservoirs offer welcome refreshment, while the **[Bergischer Panoramasteig](https://www.germany.travel/en/nature-outdoor-activities/bergisch-panorama-trail.html "Bergischer Panoramasteig")** provides varied hiking opportunities. Cultural highlights such as the Müngsten Bridge and Altenberg Cathedral complement the natural attractions.

## Upper Palatinate Forest: Tranquillity among lakes and granite rocks

![Felsenlandschaft mit einem Aussichtspunkt aus Metall, umgeben von dichten Nadelbäumen, unter blauem Himmel mit vereinzelten Wolken. Eine Metalltreppe führt zum Aussichtspunkt, auf dem mehrere Personen stehen. Die Szene spielt sich in einer bewaldeten Berglandschaft ab.](https://www.germany.travel/media/redaktion/natur_aktiv_content/saubadfelsen_im_naturpark_steinwald_oberpfaelzer_wald_thomas_kujat.jpg)**Saubadfelsen in the Steinwald Nature Park** ©Tourismusgemeinschaft Oberpfälzer Wald (Thomas Kujat)

Extensive forests, gentle uplands and numerous lakes give the **[Upper Palatinate Forest](https://www.oberpfaelzerwald.de/ "Upper Palatinate Forest")** a relaxed atmosphere. The Upper Palatinate Forest Nature Park, the Steinwald, Lake Murner See and Lake Steinberger See invite visitors to hike, cycle and spend restful hours by the water. The distinctive Doost rock formations and the ruins of Leuchtenberg Castle add scenic highlights and make the region a varied destination for a summer break.

#### What is a coolcation?

The term coolcation combines the words _cool_ and _vacation_ and describes the growing trend of spending the summer in destinations with milder temperatures. Instead of extreme heat, the focus is on shady forests, higher elevations, lakes and coastlines that offer natural ways to stay cool. Germany’s low mountain ranges provide ideal conditions, combining refreshing summer weather with a wide variety of nature experiences.
